content: Before using etonogestrel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other progestins (such as norethindrone or desogestrel), to any anesthetics or antiseptics that may be used during the procedure, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness, which can be worsened by alcohol or marijuana (cannabis). Limit your consumption of alcoholic beverages. Etonogestrel may cause blotchy, dark areas on the skin or face (melasma), which can be exacerbated by sunlight. To minimize this effect, limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen or protective clothing when outdoors. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses while using this medication. This product must not be used during pregnancy. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. Additionally, this medication can pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (such as rifampin or rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s Wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new medication and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (such as sex-hormone-binding globulin or thyroid tests), potentially causing inaccurate results. If the implant is swallowed, it may be harmful. In the event of serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
